# V1.6.4 — Photo attachments fix + sign-out crash/wedge hardening

**Status:** COMPLETE 2026-07-07. All three items committed and on-device verified by Alvin.

Reactive fix batch — not a booked/grilled batch like V1.6.1-3. Alvin reported two problems directly: photo attachments (notes + transaction receipts) upload but never show a preview and can't be expanded, and a sign-out-right-after-a-write crash that left a device looking permanently unpaired. A third, smaller request (cap note attachments at 3) rode along in the same session.

**Commits:**
1. `804da03` — sign-out wipe/cursor race + eager-`userId()` crash class
2. `182e463` — photo display fix (auth loading + partner-read RLS) + full-screen viewers + partner receipt thumbnail
3. `0664f49` — note attachment cap (3 max)

---

## Item 1 — Sign-out crash + "unpaired" wedge

- **Status:** DONE `804da03`. On-device verified by Alvin (initial repro passed only after a second round — see below).

**Alvin's report:** logged into testdev17 (paired with testdev15), uploaded a photo into a shared note, signed out within ~10 seconds — the app crashed right after showing the login screen. Signing back in showed Notes no longer shared with testdev15, and Settings → Couple showed "Create couple" / "Join couple". Tapping Create couple failed server-side with "you are already in a couple" — proving the server-side pairing was intact and only the local device had gone stale.

**Root cause (confirmed against live staging DB — both users still paired, `couple_id` intact, `server_rev` 986):**

`LocalDataWiper.wipe()` cleared Room **before** resetting the sync pull cursors, as five sequential non-atomic suspend calls, inside a `runCatching` in `AuthViewModel.performSignOut()` that silently swallowed any failure. A crash landing mid-wipe (Room already cleared, cursors still at their old high values) is unrecoverable on its own: on re-login, `EnsureCurrentUserRowUseCase`/`ensureLocalRow()` re-adopts the server's `users` row (with `couple_id` set), but `CoupleTableSyncer`'s pull (`server_rev > cursor`) never re-fetches the `couples` row or any `partner_*` rows because the stale cursor already sits above their revision — so `ObservePairingStateUseCase` sees a `couple_id` with no local `couples` row and reports `NotPaired`, permanently, until the cursors are reset by some other path (a different-user account switch, or a reinstall).

The crash itself: the auth gate flips to `Unauthenticated` the instant `client.auth.signOut()` returns, and several `observe*` Flow builders across the app resolved `CurrentUserProvider.userId()` **eagerly at flow-construction time** rather than inside the flow body. Any collector rebuilt during that brief signed-out window (confirmed via `adb logcat`: `NoteRepositoryImpl.observeNotes` via `NotesViewModel`'s `flatMapLatest`) threw `IllegalStateException` and crashed the process. This pattern existed in seven repositories, not just Notes — notes, transactions (four flows), accounts, categories, and both savings-goal repos.

**Fix:**
- `LocalDataWiper.wipe()`: cursors reset **before** Room clears — an interrupted wipe now either fully lands or leaves cursor=0 + stale Room, which self-heals on the very next pull, instead of empty-Room + stale-cursors, which wedges forever.
- `AuthViewModel`: the wipe runs under `NonCancellable`, retries once on failure (every step is idempotent), and logs instead of swallowing.
- Added `CurrentUserProvider.userIdOrNull()` and rewrote the eager-`userId()` builders in `NoteRepositoryImpl`, `TransactionRepositoryImpl` (×4), `UserRepositoryImpl` (×2), `AccountRepositoryImpl`, `CategoryRepositoryImpl`, `SavingsGoalRepositoryImpl`, and `GoalContributionRepositoryImpl` to resolve the id **inside** the flow builder, emitting empty instead of throwing when signed out.
- `CoupleChannelManager`'s debounced write→push collector (a process-lifetime scope that outlives sign-out) now skips when no authenticated user is set, so a write made just before sign-out can't fire an upload/push against a torn-down session ~1.5s later.
- Both photo uploaders (`NoteAttachmentUploader`, `ReceiptUploader`) guard their own `userId()` read with `runCatching { }.getOrNull() ?: return` so a stray post-sign-out invocation skips quietly.
- `WatchUnpairUseCase`: fixed a latent race where a wiped-then-recreated `users` row (null emission, then a fresh `coupleId = null` stub) was read as a set→null "unpair" transition and would spuriously purge the partner replica. Tracking now resets on a `null` user emission instead of treating it as a real transition.

**First test round caught a gap:** Alvin's first re-test still crashed on sign-out (same repro), which is what surfaced that the eager-`userId()` pattern existed in six *more* repositories beyond the one fixed in the initial pass — traced via `adb logcat -b crash`, which pointed straight at `NoteRepositoryImpl.observeNotes`. Second round, with all seven repos fixed, passed clean: sign-out no longer crashes, and pairing state survives repeated sign-out/sign-in cycles, including a swipe-kill of the app during the login-screen flash.

**No code recovery needed for the already-wedged testdev17 device** — the server-side couple was never touched; clearing local app data (or reinstalling) once and re-logging in converges immediately, since a cursor-0 pull re-fetches everything.

## Item 2 — Photo attachments upload but never display

- **Status:** DONE `182e463`. On-device verified by Alvin across notes (own + partner) and receipts (own + combined-view partner thumbnail), including one legacy pre-fix photo (proves the URL rewrite).

**Alvin's report:** photos in notes and transaction receipts upload successfully but show no preview and can't be tapped to view; if a note is shared, the partner should also be able to see the photo.

**Root cause #1 — private buckets, public-form URLs.** Both `note-images` and `receipts` Storage buckets are private (confirmed live: `public=false`), but `NoteAttachmentUploader`/`ReceiptUploader` stamped `publicUrl(path)` onto the row — a URL form that only resolves against a public bucket. Every image load 400'd, for the owner too.

**Root cause #2 — partner-read RLS was structurally broken.** See **ADR-0043** for the full mechanism: a `storage.objects` partner-read policy executes under the *requesting* user's own RLS, so an inline `EXISTS` subquery against an owner-scoped base table (`transactions`, or `note_images` joined to `notes`) can never see the *owner's* row — the check is always false. This was a **latent bug in the receipts policy since V1.3**, never caught because no UI exercised a partner's receipt until this batch's combined-view thumbnail. The `note-images` bucket additionally had **no Storage RLS policies at all** (owner or partner), so even the owner's own download 400'd.

Both root causes were proven directly against the live staging DB and Storage API (not simulated): the owner's authenticated download succeeded (200) while the partner's identical download 400'd, and the partner's row-match query returned `true` only when run bypassing RLS — confirming the fix target precisely before writing it.

**Fix:**
- New `StorageAuthInterceptor` (OkHttp `Interceptor`, wired into a Hilt-provided Coil `ImageLoader` that `IponApp` returns via `ImageLoaderFactory`) attaches the Supabase auth token to every Storage image request, and rewrites legacy `/object/public/` URLs already in the DB to `/object/authenticated/` form at request time — no data migration needed for existing rows.
- Both uploaders now stamp `authenticatedUrl(path)` instead of `publicUrl(path)`.
- New Storage RLS: `note_images_owner` + `note_images_partner_read` (mirroring the receipts policies), plus **rebuilt `receipts_partner_read` and `note_images_partner_read` on `SECURITY DEFINER` helper functions** (`partner_can_read_receipt`, `partner_can_read_note_image` — same technique as `auth_couple_id()`) per ADR-0043. Migration: `supabase/migrations/2026-07-07_storage_partner_read_rls.sql`, applied to staging by Alvin. Also dropped a redundant, untracked pair of `note_images_storage_*` policies found live on staging (applied via the dashboard outside any migration file at some point) — one owner + one partner-read policy per bucket now.
- Note thumbnails in the editor (`NoteEditorScreen`'s `AttachmentStrip`) are now tappable, opening a new shared `core/ui/FullScreenImageDialog` — the same component the receipt viewer (`AddTransactionScreen`) already used, now deduplicated into one composable.
- Combined view (`CombinedScreen`) now shows a small receipt thumbnail on any transaction row that has one — for both members, not just the viewer's own — tappable into the same full-screen viewer. `CombinedEntry` gained an `attachmentUrl` field, populated by `CombinedLedgerCalculator` from the underlying transaction (partner rows already carried `attachment_url` through the `partner_transactions` view; only the UI was missing).

**Explicitly out of scope (by Alvin's choice):** a notes-list attachment indicator (thumbnail/badge on the note card before opening it) was **not** added — kept minimal to loading + viewer + partner visibility.

**Scoped-out follow-up, queued separately:** receipts remain single-photo (`transactions.attachment_url`, one per row) — Alvin asked about extending them to match notes' up-to-3 multi-image pattern; that's a real vertical slice (new `transaction_images` child table, Room migration, sync ordering, partner view + RLS, swipe-scrollable UI) and was deliberately **not** folded into this batch. A ready-to-paste prompt for it was handed off for a future conversation, once this batch is committed.

## Item 3 — Cap note attachments at 3

- **Status:** DONE `0664f49`.

**Alvin's request:** notes allowed unlimited photo attachments — no ceiling on Storage cost, per-note sync/upload time, or editor memory. Requested a max of 3.

**Decision:** cap enforced in two places — `NoteEditorViewModel.addImage()` refuses a 4th attachment (backstop, `MAX_ATTACHMENTS = 3`), and the picker button in `NoteEditorScreen`'s top bar disables (greys out) once the note is at the limit, with a small `n/3` counter next to it that turns red at `3/3`. The counter only appears once a note has at least one attachment (an empty note shows just the `+` button, no `0/3` noise). Partner notes are unaffected (no add button at all — read-only). Pure client-side cap, no schema change.
